clue.text: Pantomime dame with a well-developed clutch

definitions.text: Pantomime dame with a well-developed clutch

parts.words: Pantomime dame with a well-developed clutch
parts.note: a famous pantomime role is a goose-keeping matron, and a clutch is also a batch of eggs a bird sits on, so a mother bird with a big clutch fits too

explanation.surface: A theatrical panto dame is described as having a strong grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clutch' reads as a grip or handbag, but it is the brood of eggs a hen or goose lays. Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show where a man plays the comic 'dame'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of a traditional British pantomime is a dame who is also a mother bird with eggs.

clue.text: Composition made from half of Manx cat

annotationWithheld.why: Composition made from half of Manx cat (4): no reading of half of 'Manx cat' gives OPUS; the clue as held looks garbled (perhaps half of 'octopus')
annotationWithheld.clue: Composition made from half of Manx cat

clue.text: A good headlight

parts.note: the light round the head of a good person, a saint in a painting, rather than a lamp on a car

explanation.definitionFit: A saint's nimbus is a ring of light shown around the head of a holy person in religious art.

clue.text: Most splendid and costly Rhode Island bust

parts.note: RI is the US postal abbreviation for the state of Rhode Island
the bust is the chest of the body

explanation.surface: A grand and expensive sculpture from Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wealthiest or most opulent is the most splendid and expensive.

clue.text: Solemn promise of a hot soup

indicators.note: a soup is a mixture of things stirred together, so the letters of the words before it are mixed

explanation.surface: A vow made over a bowl of hot broth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' is a noun in the surface but works as the anagram signal on the four letters of 'a hot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sworn vow is a solemn promise.

clue.text: Shifty person holding circular letter who pries into folks affairs

indicators.note: holding means the scrambled word wraps round the round letter
shifty suggests something moving about, so the letters of the next word are shifted

parts.note: O is the letter shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A shifty character with a circular in hand pokes into other people's business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifty' makes SNOPER from PERSON, and 'holding' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody who spies on others' private matters is a nosy prier.

clue.text: Get into a row when 500 satin and linen pieces fit badly

indicators.note: pieces that fit badly are jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Satin and linen pieces for a dress do not fit together well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit badly' rearranges D, SATIN and LINEN together; 'pieces' is a link word in the surface's tailoring picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To join a queue is to take one's place in a line or row.

clue.text: A heretic, maybe, but is at liberty to be one

definitions.text: A heretic, maybe, but is at liberty to be one

parts.words: A heretic, maybe, but is at liberty to be one
parts.note: a heretic rejects received doctrine, and anyone at liberty to form opinions is one who thinks without constraint

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who forms opinions independently of religious authority, as a heretic does, is an independent thinker.

clue.text: Skylight in Far East architecture

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A roof window in a Far Eastern building.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across eaST ARchitecture; 'Far' belongs to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A light in the sky is a heavenly body that shines at night.

clue.text: One point Claud makes twice, for example

indicators.note: makes is read as the letters being formed into something new

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Claud scores one point twice in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges I, POINT and CLAUD into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something twice is an instance of repetition, a copying or doubling.

clue.text: A low joint? The cap fits, naturally

definitions.text: A low joint? The cap fits, naturally

parts.words: A low joint? The cap fits, naturally
parts.note: a joint low on the leg, which wears its own bony cap, rather than a seedy bar or a hat

explanation.definitionFit: The leg's hinge between thigh and shin is covered by the patella, its natural cap.

clue.text: Dispute a hot point in these puzzles

indicators.note: in means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: these puzzles are the kind the solver is doing now
S is a compass point, south

explanation.surface: Arguing over a burning issue in the puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: S (south) goes inside the name for these puzzles, making three S's in a row; 'a hot' belongs to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight with blades is an idiom for arguing.

clue.text: Use a Foreign Office chair, perhaps, for this Dark Continent home

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for Foreign Office, the UK department for foreign affairs

explanation.surface: A Foreign Office chair might be used in an embassy building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges USE, A, FO and CHAIR. Africa House is a London building on Kingsway.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa was once called the Dark Continent, so a building named for it is its home.

clue.text: Disreputable angle taken by air force?

parts.note: RAF is the Royal Air Force
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A dubious slant taken by the military air service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angle' looks like a viewpoint, but it is fishing; 'taken by' places it after RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakish and of dubious reputation describes a person with a disreputable air.

clue.text: Marcher-like rushed about!

parts.note: rushed about in the manner of the mad animal of March, rather than a protest marcher

explanation.definitionFit: The March animal is known for wild running, so to dash like it is to run fast.

clue.text: Querulous Eve looking sickly in tossing 18

indicators.note: in places the rearranged name inside the other piece
a vessel tossing on waves is thrown about, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: the cross-reference points to 18 across, the answer meaning a vessel

indicators.note: looking sickly means out of sorts, so the name is rearranged

explanation.surface: Eve is grumpy and queasy aboard a rolling vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossing' turns SHIP into PISH; 'looking sickly' turns EVE into EEV, which goes 'in'. The printed 16 is an OCR misread of 18.
explanation.definitionFit: Querulous and peevish both mean complaining and irritable.

clue.text: Pious group who might guide us to the heavens

definitions.text: who might guide us to the heavens

parts.note: PI is a short informal word for pious
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A devout congregation leading worshippers heavenward.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator flies an aircraft and so steers passengers up into the sky.

clue.text: Twisty-nosed hoofer disorganising a trip

indicators.note: disorganising means putting into disorder, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A dancer with a crooked nose messes up a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoofer' suggests a dancer, but it is a hoofed animal with a flexible snout.
explanation.definitionFit: This hoofed mammal has a mobile, trunk-like nose it can twist.

clue.text: Despatch his troublesome page

indicators.note: troublesome means the word is unruly, so its letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Send off his difficult young attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: To send goods off is to dispatch them.

clue.text: A detailed plant scheme

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, with the final letter cut off

explanation.surface: A thorough scheme for planting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' means having its tail removed, so PLANT loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a design or programme of action.

clue.text: Serpentine poison making nautical leader move about awkwardly

indicators.note: moved about awkwardly means jumbled, so the letters are reordered
the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A snake's toxin forces the ship's captain to shift clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes N from 'nautical', and 'about awkwardly' mixes it with MOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakes inject a toxic fluid through their fangs.

clue.text: Very old chopped tree S stowed into vehicle

indicators.note: stowed into means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle

indicators.note: chopped means cut up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letters

explanation.surface: An ancient felled tree is loaded into a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' turns TREE into ETER, which is 'stowed into' VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-serving, old hand is one of great age and experience.

clue.text: Orville, perhaps, sounds like the chap she's been waiting 0 for

definitions.text: the chap she's been waiting 0 for

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the title and surname are said out loud

parts.note: Orville Wright, pioneer aviator, would be addressed as Mr Wright

explanation.surface: A woman waits for a man named Orville.
explanation.walkthrough: Orville is one of the Wright brothers who flew the first powered aeroplane; the printed 0 is a stray OCR mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The ideal partner a woman hopes to meet is the perfect man.

clue.text: Late starter skated round and followed

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the letters are rearranged
a starter is the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A latecomer skated around and chased after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' gives L from 'Late', and 'round' mixes it with SKATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue stealthily is to track or follow.

clue.text: Shower interrupts start of golf round for the learner

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into the other piece

parts.note: each hole of golf begins from the tee
a shower is a spell of rain

explanation.surface: A downpour halts the opening of a golf round for a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of golf round' looks like a first letter G, but it is the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in training is a learner.

clue.text: Get a revolutionary highball with nothing but an old Greek coin

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned right round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a lob is a high ball in tennis or cricket

explanation.surface: Get a drink and nothing else but an ancient coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highball' suggests a whisky drink, but it is a lob; 'revolutionary' turns it to BOL.
explanation.definitionFit: This small silver piece was currency in ancient Athens.

clue.text: A net woven for poker players?

indicators.note: woven means interlaced, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A knitted net for card players.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake each poker player puts in before the deal is the pot money for them.

clue.text: Rice ordered for Morecambe

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are put in another sequence

explanation.surface: A rice dish requested in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire seaside town, but it is Eric Morecambe, the British comedian of Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic half of a famous British double act had the stage surname of the town.

clue.text: Beware of highly explosive boss on paper

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Watch out for a fiery newspaper chief.
explanation.definitionFit: To take notice of a warning is to be wary of it.

clue.text: By the way, this little Eden can't be reached by back-door methods

definitions.text: By the way, this little Eden can't be reached by back-door methods

parts.words: By the way, this little Eden can't be reached by back-door methods
parts.note: a little paradise beside the road, at the house's face, which you would not reach through the rear door

explanation.definitionFit: The plot of lawn and flowers before a house lies by the street, not behind.

clue.text: A record I'd turn over to science

indicators.note: turn over means flip the letters to run backwards

parts.note: the contraction gives the two letters I and D
SC is an abbreviation for science

explanation.surface: A record I would hand over to the scientists.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl record is a flat round platter.

clue.text: Possible fly-killer in body? One detective department gets the point

parts.note: a sect is a body of believers
I is the Roman numeral one
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A fly spray in the body, and a detective unit gets the point.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug spray poisons pests such as flies.
